newsitem.title: UK: UK corporate tax changes no aid to investment - IFS.
newsitem.headline: UK corporate tax changes no aid to investment - IFS.

text.p: Changes to Britain's corporate tax regime, unveiled on Wednesday by Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown in his first budget, will be little if any help to investment as he claims, the Institute for Fiscal Studies said.
While giving with one hand he has taken more away with the other.
Brown cut corporation tax by two percentage points to 31 percent. That would add about two billion pounds to corporate profits, Stephen Bond at the IFS said.

But the abolition of tax credits on Advance Corporation Tax, hitherto paid to pension funds and other institutions who are exempt from the tax, took five billion pounds out of the business sector, he said.
"Despite Gordon Brown's rhetoric, it is difficult to see how the changes will help investment," Bond said in a post-budget briefing.
Brown told parliament that the corporation tax cut will boost investment while the cut in tax credits would do the same -- lessening the bias towards hefty dividend payouts.
But Bond said companies will still come under pressure to pay out large dividends. "Indeed they will be pressured to make up a substantial party of the five billion in lost revenues."
To make the changes in corporation tax fiscally neutral would have required the overall rate to be cut to 28 percent not 31, he said.
